items.title: Japan to ship carbon emissions to Malaysia in regional first

featured_image.name: Malaysia and Japan plan major cross-border carbon capture project ...

items.description:
Japan will ship carbon dioxide emissions to Malaysia in what would be the first cross-border carbon capture and storage project in Southeast Asia, a plan that is drawing criticism from climate advocates who argue the technology is more symbolic than effective in combating climate change.

Under the arrangement, emissions from Japan's polluting industries—including electric power, oil refining, cement, and steel—would be captured, liquefied, and transported by ship to depleted gas fields off the coast of Sarawak on the island of Borneo. If successful, experts say the project could pave the way for similar initiatives in other Southeast Asian nations such as Indonesia and Thailand.[1]

items.title: Kremlin rejects European findings that Russia poisoned Navalny

featured_image.name: Alexei Navalny, in his own words

items.description:
Scientists and chemical weapons experts conclude that the rare neurotoxin found in Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny's body was almost certainly synthesized in a laboratory rather than harvested from South American dart frogs, according to analysis released at the Munich Security Conference last week.

The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands announced on February 14 that laboratory testing had "conclusively confirmed" the presence of epibatidine in samples taken from Navalny's body. The toxin, naturally occurring only in Ecuadorian poison dart frogs, was described as "highly likely" the cause of his death in an Arctic penal colony on February 16, 2024.[1][2][3]

items.title: EU advisers warn bloc unprepared for worsening climate change

featured_image.name: Ottmar Edenhofer reappointed to the EU Climate Advisory ...

items.description:
The European Union is unprepared for worsening climate change and must urgently increase investment to protect people and infrastructure from intensifying floods, wildfires, and severe heatwaves, independent scientific advisers warned on Monday.

The European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change released a report titled "Strengthening resilience to climate change – Recommendations for an effective EU adaptation policy framework," calling for a more coordinated approach across member states as the bloc faces escalating climate risks that could "undermine the EU's economic and social foundations."[1][2]

items.title: Bacteria frozen 5,000 years in Romanian cave resists 10 antibiotics

featured_image.name: This ancient bacterium could help solve the antibiotic ...

items.description: A bacterial strain preserved for 5,000 years in the ice of Romania's Scarisoara Cave has been found resistant to 10 modern antibiotics, according to research published this week in Frontiers in Microbiology. The discovery offers new insights into the ancient origins of antimicrobial resistance while raising concerns about the potential spread of resistance genes as climate change melts long-frozen environments.

items.title: China's clean energy capacity surpasses fossil fuels for first time

featured_image.name: China is installing the wind and solar equivalent of five ...

items.description:
China has crossed a historic threshold in its energy transition, with clean energy sources now accounting for more installed power capacity than fossil fuels for the first time, according to new data from Global Energy Monitor. As of February 2026, 52% of China's operating power capacity comes from non-fossil fuel sources, while 48% is derived from coal, natural gas, and other fossil fuels.[1][2][3]

The milestone places the world's largest carbon emitter alongside Brazil, France, and Germany as economies predominantly powered by clean energy. Yet China's continued construction of coal-fired power plants at record levels underscores the tensions between its climate ambitions and energy security concerns.

items.title: Oil holds steady as US-Iran nuclear talks resume in Geneva

featured_image.name: Iran launches naval drills ahead of US nuclear talks

items.description:
Oil prices held steady on Tuesday as traders weighed supply disruption risks following Iranian naval exercises near the Strait of Hormuz, with attention focused on high-stakes nuclear talks between the United States and Iran set to begin later in the day in Geneva.

Brent crude futures edged lower by 0.2 percent, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate held near Monday's closing levels, according to Reuters. Market participants are watching whether the negotiations could ease tensions or set the stage for further escalation in a region that accounts for roughly a fifth of global oil shipments.[1][2]

items.title: Report finds 74% of Big Tech's AI climate claims lack evidence

featured_image.name: Google blames AI for growing emissions that threaten its climate goals

items.description:
A new analysis has found that the vast majority of claims from technology companies about artificial intelligence's potential to combat climate change are unsupported by evidence, with researchers warning that the energy-intensive nature of generative AI may actually worsen global emissions.

The report, released on February 17 by climate nonprofits Beyond Fossil Fuels and Climate Action Against Disinformation, examined 154 statements from industry and institutional sources claiming AI would deliver net climate benefits. According to the study, 74 percent of these assertions lacked any verifiable evidence.[1][2]

items.title: Trump to participate 'indirectly' in Iran nuclear talks in Geneva

featured_image.name: Trump says he will be involved ‘indirectly’ in Iran nuclear talks

items.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Geneva on Monday ahead of a second round of indirect nuclear negotiations with the United States, meeting with the head of the U.N. nuclear watchdog as both sides signaled cautious willingness to engage while holding firm to core positions.

The talks, scheduled for Tuesday and mediated by Oman, come amid heightened military posturing in the Persian Gulf and volatile commodity markets. President Donald Trump said he would participate "indirectly" in the negotiations, calling them "very important" while asserting that Tehran is eager to reach a deal following U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities last June.[1][2]

items.title: NASA says 15,000 city-killer asteroids remain undetected

featured_image.name: Asteroid that will spare Earth might hit the moon instead, according ...

items.description:
NASA's head of planetary defense has acknowledged that approximately 15,000 medium-sized asteroids capable of devastating an entire city remain undetected and untracked, leaving Earth vulnerable to a potentially catastrophic strike with little warning.

Dr. Kelly Fast, the agency's Acting Planetary Defense Officer, made the admission at the American Association for the Advancement of Science annual meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, which concluded on February 14. She said NASA has only identified about 40 percent of the estimated 25,000 near-Earth asteroids that are at least 140 meters in diameter, the threshold scientists consider capable of causing major regional devastation.[1][2]

"It's truly the asteroids we are unaware of that keep me up at night," Fast said. "We aren't particularly concerned about the larger ones featured in movies since we know their locations. The smaller objects are constantly entering our atmosphere, and I'm not excessively worried about them. It's the intermediate-sized asteroids that could cause regional damage—while not necessarily global consequences—that truly concern us. And we have no idea where all of them are."[2]

items.title: Trash piles up in Havana as US oil sanctions cripple Cuba

featured_image.name: Trash overwhelms Havana as garbage trucks lack parts, fuel

items.description:
Garbage is piling up on street corners across Havana, attracting swarms of flies and emitting the stench of rotting food, as Washington's campaign to cut off oil supplies to Cuba cripples the capital's waste collection system.

Only 44 of Havana's 106 garbage trucks remain operational due to fuel shortages, state media outlet Cubadebate reported this month, according to Reuters. Cardboard boxes, plastic bottles, used bags, and rags now tower at intersections throughout the coastal city, forcing motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists to navigate around the refuse.[1]

"It's all over the city," resident Jose Ramon Cruz told Reuters. "It's been more than 10 days since a garbage truck came."[1]
